newsitem.title: GERMANY: German politicians face shuttle to and from Berlin.
newsitem.headline: German politicians face shuttle to and from Berlin.

text.p: German politicians face months of shuttling 600 km (375 miles) between Bonn and Berlin in 1999 because deputies' offices will not be ready in time to house them, though the newly-refurbished parliament building will be.

On Friday the Council of Elders of the lower house decided that plenary sessions would be held in Berlin as planned from May 1999 onwards as part of the government's and parliament's move to Berlin, agreed after German unification in 1990.
But it said other parliamentary business might have to be carried out in Bonn until new committee rooms and deputies' offices, due to be complete in December 1999, were finished.

The government is also due to take up residence in Berlin by May 1999, when the election of a new president will mark the re-inauguration of the Reichstag building, home of the parliament before Adolf Hitler came to power in 1933.
But with some ministers due to stay in Bonn, and others keeping an office in Berlin while their administration remains in Bonn, the flow of commuters between the old and new capitals looks assured.
